server_scripts.name: GitHub Tool: Read Pull Request
Orchestrator Agent: Read the Work Item
server_scripts.script:
# Orchestrator Agent - Read the Work Item.
# This map runs as a SUB-PROCESS of Software Development, so the instance context
# is already the Work Item that was flagged for the orchestrator.
#
# The Work Item is resolved from context_docname rather than from `doc`. `doc` is
# the trigger document, and it is only reliably the Work Item when the whole
# instance runs in one pass from the record insert. Once the map gained the
# reporter's Open Work Item and Start Work gates, the agent runs on a LATER pass
# resumed by a person completing a task, and `doc` no longer carried the Work
# Item - so title and description came back blank, the user prompt rendered
# empty, and the agent politely asked for a brief that the process had failed to
# give it. Nothing errored, which is what made it hard to see.
if context_doctype != "Work Item" or not context_docname:
    frappe.throw(
        "Orchestrator: expected a Work Item as this instance's context, got "
        + str(context_doctype) + " " + str(context_docname)
    )

wi = frappe.get_doc("Work Item", context_docname)
title = (wi.title or "").strip()
body = frappe.utils.strip_html(wi.description or "").strip()

brief = title
if body:
    brief = title + "\n\n" + body

# Loud on purpose. An empty brief used to reach the model as an empty user
# prompt, and the agent's reply ("no work item content was provided") read like
# an agent problem rather than a process one.
if not brief:
    frappe.throw(
        "Orchestrator: Work Item " + str(context_docname)
        + " has no title or description to work from."
    )

state = (wi.workflow_state or wi.status or "").strip()
pr_link = (wi.pr_link or "").strip()
target_app = (wi.get("target_app") or "").strip()
git_branch = (wi.get("git_branch") or "").strip()
# The app and branch are fields on the Work Item, not something to infer from the
# description. Named in the header so the model passes them on as given; when the
# reporter left one blank the header says so, and the specialist falls back to its
# own rules instead of receiving an invented value.
header = "Work Item: " + wi.name + "\nState: " + state + ("\nPull request: " + pr_link if pr_link else "")
header += "\nType: " + (wi.work_item_type or "not set on the work item")
header += "\nTarget app: " + (target_app or "not set on the work item")
header += "\nBranch: " + (git_branch or "not set on the work item") + "\n\n"
result["work_item"] = context_docname
result["work_item_type"] = wi.work_item_type
result["work_item_state"] = state
result["pull_request"] = pr_link
result["target_app"] = target_app
result["git_branch"] = git_branch
result["work_item_brief"] = header + brief

# The "Needs to call tools?" gateway reads this. Pinned False for the same reason
# every other agent map pins it: the AI Agent Task runs its own tool loop
# internally, so the flow past the gateway never re-enters the Tools sub-process.
result["needs_tools"] = False

server_scripts.name: Orchestrator Agent: Record the Outcome
server_scripts.script:
# Orchestrator Agent — Record the Outcome. # There is no A2A Task to answer here: the caller is the Software Development # instance this map runs inside, so the report goes back as workflow data and is # written onto the Work Item as a comment so the trail outlives the instance. # # Nothing here sets a Work Item FIELD. Status is the Software Development process's # business — the orchestrator reporting its own outcome into `status` would race the # very steps that called it. report = (task_data.get("ai_result") or "").strip() if not report: report = "The orchestrator produced no report." # `connector_result` is the delegate shape's resultVariable. It is absent when the # orchestrator decided no specialist applied, which is a real outcome, not an error. delegated = task_data.get("connector_result") result["orchestrator_report"] = report result["orchestrator_delegated_to"] = "Connector Agent" if delegated else None # Attributed to the AGENT, not to whoever started the run. # # This script runs on the engine's path, which switches to the person who # triggered the instance — right for a business process's own script tasks, wrong # for a script inside an agent's map. The result was two comments a paragraph # apart, both from the orchestrator, signed by two different parties: this report # under a human's name and the tool's comment under the agent's. # # `agent_configuration` is injected by the engine and is empty for an ordinary # process, in which case this falls back to the old behaviour. from one_bpmn.agents import identity if agent_configuration: identity.comment_as( agent_configuration, context_doctype, context_docname, "Orchestrator
" + frappe.utils.escape_html(report), ) else: doc.add_comment("Comment", "Orchestrator
" + frappe.utils.escape_html(report))

server_scripts.name: Work Item Tool: Hand Back to a Person
server_scripts.script:
# Give the work back to a person and stop being its owner. if context_doctype != "Work Item" or not context_docname: frappe.throw("This tool only works on a Work Item, and this run has none.") # The agent's own permission, checked HERE rather than left to whatever the # helper underneath happens to do. frappe.get_doc does not check read at all and # save() can be told to ignore permissions, so an agent granted nothing could # otherwise reassign a work item. frappe.has_permission("Work Item", "write", doc=context_docname, throw=True) why = (task_data.get("reason") or "").strip() item = frappe.get_doc("Work Item", context_docname) # WHO, when the agent does not know who. # # Naming somebody used to be mandatory, and the agent had no way to find one: # nothing in its brief names a person and it has no tool that lists them. So on # the first work item that genuinely needed a human it reasoned its way to the # right answer, wrote "this needs to go to a person" in its report, asked who -- # in prose, which reaches nobody -- and handed it over to nobody. The item sat # with the orchestrator still on it. # # So naming somebody is optional now, and leaving it out means the person who # raised the item. They asked for it, so they are the one who can say where it # should go next, and they are always there. assignee = (task_data.get("assignee") or "").strip() if not assignee: assignee = item.get("reporter_user") or item.get("process_owner") or item.owner result["chose_the_reporter"] = 1 if not assignee or not frappe.db.exists("User", assignee): frappe.throw( "There is nobody to hand this to - " + (assignee or "this work item names no reporter") + " is not a user. Name somebody who is." ) item.assignee_user = assignee item.orchestrator = 0 item.save() item.add_comment( "Comment", "Handed back to a person
Assigned to " + frappe.utils.escape_html(assignee) + (("
" + frappe.utils.escape_html(why)) if why else "") ) result["assigned_to"] = assignee result["orchestrator_cleared"] = 1 # Tell the person. The comment above only reaches somebody who is already # looking at the record, and the whole point of a hand-back is that the # orchestrator has STOPPED and a human now has to act — so it has to arrive # somewhere they will see it. Without this the item simply went quiet: the # orchestrator came off it, nobody was told, and it waited. # # is_external_mail=True for the same reason the BPMN "Notify Assignee" path # passes it: one_fm's recipient filter drops any user who is not an Active # Employee with their user_id set as the preferred Company Email contact, and # the mail then vanishes with no error. A hand-back is an explicit act aimed at # one person, not a subscription, so their general notification preferences must # not decide whether it arrives. notice_link = frappe.utils.get_url_to_form("Work Item", item.name) notice_subject = "Handed back to you: " + item.name notice_parts = [ "

The orchestrator has stopped work on " + frappe.utils.escape_html(item.name) + " and handed it to you.

", ] if item.title: notice_parts.append("

" + frappe.utils.escape_html(item.title) + "

") if why: notice_parts.append("

Why: " + frappe.utils.escape_html(why) + "

") if result.get("chose_the_reporter"): # Say so plainly: being picked by fallback rather than by name changes what # the recipient should do — the first question is who this really belongs to. notice_parts.append( "

Nobody was named, so this came to you as the person who raised it." " If it belongs with somebody else, please reassign it.

" ) notice_parts.append( '

Open ' + frappe.utils.escape_html(item.name) + "

" ) notice_body = "".join(notice_parts) result["notified"] = 0 try: try: from one_fm.processor import sendemail as onefm_sendemail onefm_sendemail( recipients=[assignee], subject=notice_subject, header=[notice_subject], message=notice_body, reference_doctype="Work Item", reference_name=item.name, is_external_mail=True, ) except ImportError: frappe.sendmail( recipients=[assignee], subject=notice_subject, message=notice_body, reference_doctype="Work Item", reference_name=item.name, ) result["notified"] = assignee except Exception: # Never fail the hand-back over its own notification. The item HAS already # moved and been saved; throwing here would report the handoff as failed and # invite the agent to retry it, reassigning something already assigned. frappe.log_error( title="Work Item hand-back notification failed", message=frappe.get_traceback(), )

server_scripts.name: Work Item Tool: Move the State
server_scripts.script:
# Move the Work Item's state, but only to a state this shape permits.
#
# Free-form would be a second authority over a field the process owns: Software
# Development moves it with apply_workflow tasks that carry role guards, and the
# reporter's Open and Start Work gates sit in front of them. A tool that could set
# any state, Done included, would walk past all of that.
#
# So the shape declares what is allowed and this refuses anything else, and the
# move itself goes through the same helper the process uses, so onlyAllowEdit and
# the workflow comment still apply.
if context_doctype != "Work Item" or not context_docname:
    frappe.throw("This tool only works on a Work Item, and this run has none.")

# The agent's own permission, checked HERE rather than left to whatever the
# helper underneath happens to do. Two of these tools slipped straight past the
# gate when it was implicit: frappe.get_doc does not check read at all,
# add_comment inserts with permissions ignored, and the workflow helper saves the
# same way. So an agent granted nothing could still annotate a work item and move
# its state — which is the opposite of the point.
frappe.has_permission("Work Item", "write", doc=context_docname, throw=True)

target = (task_data.get("state") or "").strip()
allowed_raw = (shape_config.get("allowed_states") or "").strip()
allowed = [s.strip() for s in allowed_raw.split(",") if s.strip()]

if not allowed:
    frappe.throw(
        "This shape declares no permitted states, so it cannot move anything. "
        "Set allowedStates on the tool shape."
    )
if not target:
    frappe.throw("Name the state to move to. Permitted here: " + ", ".join(allowed))
if target not in allowed:
    frappe.throw(
        "This tool may not set '" + target + "'. It is limited to: " + ", ".join(allowed)
        + ". That is a deliberate limit on the shape, not a transient failure."
    )

from one_bpmn.api.workflow_state import _apply_bpmn_workflow_state

_apply_bpmn_workflow_state(
    doctype="Work Item",
    docname=context_docname,
    target_state=target,
    doc_status_hint="0",
    triggered_by=frappe.session.user,
)

result["moved_to"] = target
result["work_item"] = context_docname

server_scripts.name: Work Item Tool: Record a Comment
server_scripts.script:
# Put something on the record. The one tool that is purely additive: it changes
# no field, so it cannot fail validation, and what an agent has worked out is
# worth keeping even when nothing else about the item changes.
if context_doctype != "Work Item" or not context_docname:
    frappe.throw("This tool only works on a Work Item, and this run has none.")

# The agent's own permission, checked HERE rather than left to whatever the
# helper underneath happens to do. Two of these tools slipped straight past the
# gate when it was implicit: frappe.get_doc does not check read at all,
# add_comment inserts with permissions ignored, and the workflow helper saves the
# same way. So an agent granted nothing could still annotate a work item and move
# its state — which is the opposite of the point.
frappe.has_permission("Work Item", "write", doc=context_docname, throw=True)

text = (task_data.get("comment") or "").strip()
if not text:
    frappe.throw("There is nothing to record — pass the comment text.")

item = frappe.get_doc("Work Item", context_docname)
item.add_comment("Comment", frappe.utils.escape_html(text[:4000]))

result["commented_on"] = context_docname
result["by"] = frappe.session.user

server_scripts.name: Work Item Tool: What This Relates To
server_scripts.script:
# What this Work Item relates to: its epic, its sprint siblings, anything linked.
#
# Deliberately NOT a "read this work item" tool. The map already put the brief in
# the prompt; fetching it again would spend a tool-calling turn on data the agent
# was handed, and a turn is scarce enough that a worker capped at one produced no
# answer at all.
if context_doctype != "Work Item" or not context_docname:
    frappe.throw("This tool only works on a Work Item, and this run has none.")

# Read is the honest requirement for a lookup, and it is checked explicitly for
# the same reason: frappe.get_doc enforces nothing on its own.
frappe.has_permission("Work Item", "read", doc=context_docname, throw=True)

item = frappe.get_doc("Work Item", context_docname)

epic = None
if item.epic:
    epic_doc = frappe.get_doc("Work Item", item.epic)
    epic = {"name": epic_doc.name, "title": epic_doc.title, "status": epic_doc.status}

siblings = []
if item.sprint:
    for row in frappe.get_all(
        "Work Item",
        filters={"sprint": item.sprint, "name": ["!=", item.name]},
        fields=["name", "title", "status", "assignee_user", "story_points"],
        order_by="name",
        limit=20,
    ):
        siblings.append(row)

children = []
for row in frappe.get_all(
    "Work Item",
    filters={"epic": item.name},
    fields=["name", "title", "status"],
    order_by="name",
    limit=20,
):
    children.append(row)

result["epic"] = epic
result["sprint"] = item.sprint
result["sprint_siblings"] = siblings
result["items_under_this_epic"] = children
result["counts"] = {
    "siblings": len(siblings),
    "children": len(children),
}
